title: Finite reduction of a fixed-point stalk identification
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and integers $N\geq j\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^N$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^j$, with the quotient map $A\to B$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the constant-coefficient small pro-etale derived categories and $D^b_{ctf}$ conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. For a complex $M$ write $rM=M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$, using derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $h:X\to X$ be a $k$-endomorphism and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Write $Lh_A^*$ and $Lh_B^*$ for derived pullback at the two coefficient rings [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $\mu_{h,K}:r(Lh_A^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_B^*(rK)$ for the canonical coefficient/pullback comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction].

Let $\bar y:t=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and suppose the scheme maps satisfy $h\circ\bar y=\bar y$. Set
$$
S_R(M)=\Gamma\bigl(t,L\bar y_R^*M\bigr)\in D(R),\qquad R=A,B,
$$
using exact derived sections at the algebraically closed point [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Let
$$
\iota_{h,R,M}:S_R(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_R(Lh_R^*M)
$$
be sections of the pullback-composition isomorphism $L(h\circ\bar y)_R^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}L\bar y_R^*Lh_R^*M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with its source identified with $L\bar y_R^*M$ using $h\circ\bar y=\bar y$.
For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ let $\sigma_M:rS_A(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_B(rM)$ be the point-sections reduction isomorphism [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] followed by sections of the coefficient/pullback comparison for $\bar y$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Since $Lh_A^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by clause (i) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], $\sigma_{Lh_A^*K}$ is defined; set $\widetilde\sigma_K=S_B(\mu_{h,K})\circ\sigma_{Lh_A^*K}$. Then
$$
\widetilde\sigma_K\circ r(\iota_{h,A,K})=\iota_{h,B,rK}\circ\sigma_K
\quad\text{in }D(B).
$$
This identity is natural in $K$ and assumes no Weil structure, no coefficient endomorphism and no properness of $h$.

proof.text: Put $P_R=L\bar y_R^*$, $H_R=Lh_R^*$, and let $r_T$ denote derived change of rings on a scheme $T$ (with $r$ for ordinary coefficient complexes). For $f:U\to V$ write $\lambda_{f,M}:r_U(Lf_A^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf_B^*(r_VM)$ for the canonical coefficient/pullback comparison; thus $\lambda_{h,K}=\mu_{h,K}$. It is the inverse tensor/pullback comparison with the constant $A$-module sheaf $B$, interpreted as a $B$-linear comparison by derived change of rings. The finite-level definitions identify pullbacks with exact termwise inverse image, so $P_A M$ is bounded above when $M$ is bounded above. The composition theorem gives $d_{R,M}=c_{\bar y,h,R,M}:P_R M\to P_RH_RM$ after using $h\bar y=\bar y$. Applying exact sections gives precisely $\iota_{h,R,M}=\Gamma(t,d_{R,M})$.

proof.text:
Apply the composition compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] with $f=h$, the second map $\bar y$, and tensor arguments $K$ and the constant coefficient sheaf $B$. Use the canonical identifications of each pullback of $B$ with the constant sheaf $B$. With $\eta_M=\lambda_{\bar y,M}:r_tP_AM\to P_B(r_XM)$, that compatibility reads
$$
 P_B(\mu_{h,K})\circ\eta_{H_AK}\circ r_t(d_{A,K})
 =d_{B,r_XK}\circ\eta_K.
$$
Indeed the composite-map comparison $\lambda_{h\bar y,K}$ becomes $\lambda_{\bar y,K}=\eta_K$ under $h\bar y=\bar y$, and the target composition comparison is $d_{B,r_XK}$. This uses the tensor lemma's explicit composition clause, rather than attributing a composition clause to [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. All maps here are the canonical derived change-of-rings maps: on the tensor representatives they preserve the $B$ action, and the tensor-composition identity is an identity of these $B$-linear maps before localization. Hence the displayed equation is in $D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, not merely after forgetting coefficients.

proof.text:
For a bounded-above point complex $Q$ let $\tau_Q:r\Gamma(t,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(t,r_tQ)$ be the natural comparison of [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction]. Apply its naturality to the point-complex map $d_{A,K}:P_AK\to P_AH_AK$:
$$
 \Gamma(t,r_t(d_{A,K}))\circ\tau_{P_AK}
 =\tau_{P_AH_AK}\circ r\Gamma(t,d_{A,K}).
$$
Both inputs are bounded above because $K$ is bounded and the two finite-coefficient pullbacks are exact. By definition $\sigma_M=\Gamma(t,\eta_M)\circ\tau_{P_AM}$. Apply $\Gamma(t,-)$ to the equation of step 2, precompose with $\tau_{P_AK}$, and use the displayed naturality equation. The result is
$$
 S_B(\mu_{h,K})\circ\sigma_{H_AK}\circ r(\iota_{h,A,K})
 =\iota_{h,B,rK}\circ\sigma_K
$$
in $D(B)$. This uses naturality of $\tau$ on point complexes, not an assertion that $d_{A,K}$ is the pullback of a morphism on $X$.

proof.text: The morphism $h$ is separated and finite type: a $k$-map between separated finite-type $k$-schemes has closed graph, so it factors as its graph followed by the finite-type separated projection $X\times_kX\to X$. Clause (i) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] therefore gives $H_AK\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, as required by the notation $\sigma_{H_AK}$ in the statement. Substitute $\widetilde\sigma_K=S_B(\mu_{h,K})\circ\sigma_{H_AK}$ in step 3. Each map used there is natural in $K$ (the composition isomorphism, the tensor/pullback comparisons, and $\tau$); thus the identity is natural in $K$. The argument used only the equality $h\bar y=\bar y$ and the stated coefficient and domain hypotheses, with no Weil structure, coefficient endomorphism, or properness of $h$.
